subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw replace the shipped `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` session archive convention plus retention deletion behavior with a permanent archive naming or directory model, and what migration and purge policy should existing users get?
rationale: Source inspection proves the current behavior, but choosing new suffixes, archive location, compatibility handling, and disk-budget purge semantics is a user-facing storage contract decision.

options.title: Adopt archive contract with migration
options.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and keep physical purge behind an explicit documented retention setting.

options.title: Clarify current behavior
options.body: Leave existing suffixes and cleanup behavior intact, but document that `.deleted.*` means detached until retention or disk budget removes it.

options.title: Split terminology from no-delete policy
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/80263 for naming/config clarity and track the no-physical-delete durability policy as separate product work.

recommendation.title: Adopt archive contract with migration
recommendation.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and keep physical purge behind an explicit documented retention setting.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session product work makes this the best available owner for the user-facing lifecycle contract choice.
